read: On 35 fixed cases (24 Q4 solo-wrong), the flash-lite holdout adopts the wrong answer 0.3429 under two unanimous wrong peers but only 0.1714 when one of the two instead asserts the CORRECT answer (a single dissenter), a directional reduction of 0.1715. This is CONSISTENT with the classic Asch finding that a single ally breaks conformity (the deference depends on a unanimous board), but it is NOT significant at this sample size (paired McNemar gain=7 lose=1, p=0.070312; only 8 discordant cases) across the fixed cohort. Reported honestly as a suggestive-but-underpowered dissenter effect; a larger solo-wrong pool (or a lower-baseline-accuracy set) would be needed to confirm it.
